meta.title: Transfer Photos from iPhone to PC — Full Quality, No Cable | BIShare
meta.description: Move photos from iPhone to a Windows PC over Wi-Fi at full resolution — no cable, no iTunes, no iCloud subscription. HEIC, Live Photos, and 4K video arrive untouched.

hero.title: Transfer photos from iPhone to PC without a cable
hero.body: Your camera roll deserves better than a frayed Lightning cable and a Photos-app import that dies at 43%. BIShare sends your photos and videos from iPhone straight to your PC over Wi-Fi — full resolution, HEIC and Live Photos intact, hundreds at a time. The PC side can receive in a plain browser, no install needed.

why.title: Why the usual ways butcher your photos
why.body: The cable route depends on drivers, trust prompts, and a Photos importer that chokes on large libraries. iCloud wants a monthly subscription the moment you pass 5 GB — and if "Optimize Storage" is on, the full-quality originals aren't even on your phone anymore. Email caps you at a few megabytes, and chat apps quietly recompress every image into mush. None of these problems are about your photos; they're about the route. Change the route and they disappear.

how.title: How BIShare moves your camera roll

0.b: Open BIShare on the iPhone, pick photos, tap your PC. Files travel directly between the two machines, end-to-end encrypted — nothing is uploaded anywhere. Originals arrive byte-for-byte: full resolution, EXIF and location data intact.

1.b: Multi-select in your camera roll and send the whole batch in one go — it lands in a single folder on the PC, at local Wi-Fi speed. A vacation's worth of photos takes minutes, not an evening.

2.b: Turn on the iPhone's hotspot and the PC joins it — the transfer runs with zero internet. Or send an expiring link instead: the PC downloads from any browser, wherever it is.

rows.r0: No cable, drivers, or trust prompts
rows.r1: Free at any library size — no 5 GB wall
rows.r3: Photos on the PC in minutes, not an overnight sync

0.q: Do my photos lose quality during the transfer?
0.a: No. BIShare moves the original files byte-for-byte — full resolution, no recompression, EXIF and location data intact. A 48 MP ProRAW arrives as a 48 MP ProRAW.

1.q: How do I open HEIC photos on Windows?
1.a: Windows 10 and 11 open HEIC with Microsoft's free HEIF Image Extensions. Prefer JPEGs everywhere? Set iPhone Settings → Camera → Formats to "Most Compatible" and new photos are captured as JPEG. BIShare transfers either format unchanged.

2.q: Can I transfer my entire camera roll at once?
2.a: You can multi-select and send very large batches in one transfer — the practical limit is your PC's disk, not the app. For libraries with many thousands of photos, sending in a few large batches keeps things easy to verify.

3.q: Does my PC need BIShare installed?
3.a: No — on the same network, your PC can receive in any browser at bishare.app/transfer. Installing the Windows app is worth it for big batches: it's faster and photos land straight in a folder you choose.

4.q: What about Live Photos and 4K videos?
4.a: A Live Photo is a photo plus a short video, and both parts transfer. 4K video moves at local Wi-Fi speed with no size cap on the direct route — a multi-gigabyte clip is routine, not a special case.

cta.title: Your camera roll, on your PC tonight
cta.body: Free, end-to-end encrypted, and faster than finding that cable ever was.
